concepts.def: Charter limiting King John's power; clause 39 established no free man should be imprisoned except by lawful judgment.
Baron who summoned first parliament including commoners (knights and burgesses) after defeating Henry III at Lewes.
War between Charles I (Royalists) and Parliament (Roundheads); ended with Charles's execution in January 1649.
Constitutional law after Glorious Revolution limiting monarchy and establishing parliamentary sovereignty.
Cavalry charge into crowd of 60,000 demanding parliamentary reform at St Peter's Field, Manchester; 18 killed.
Working class movement demanding six points including universal male suffrage and secret ballot; three petitions failed.
